comments.text: We Italians often engage in self-criticism—the only other country where I’ve seen this happen is England. We return and want to stay because of our culture; we possess a language that, counting all its variations and nuances, boasts over two million words. We are a people who love to indulge ourselves. When we are abroad, after a while, we can’t wait to come back; we miss the aroma of tomatoes and basil on our pasta, and the scent of morning coffee. We are a people who love our comforts. But believe me—having lived abroad—I have never found a people with such rich culture and history, or such heartwarming traditions involving family, friends, and genuine warmth. When does a nation become your home? When the people around you love you and embrace you warmly. That is what makes it home. So, dear British and American friends: come visit.
